subject: general
question: If sin x = cos(5x - 60°), then what is the value of x?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When sin A = cos B, their angles are complementary, meaning A + B = 90°.

⇒ x + 5x − 60° = 90°

⇒ 6x = 150°

⇒ x = 25°

**∴ The correct answer is 25°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

sin x = cos(5x − 60°)

**Formula Used:**

sin θ = cos(90° − θ)

**Calculations:**

⇒ cos(90° − x) = cos(5x − 60°)

Equating the angles on both sides:

⇒ 90° − x = 5x − 60°

⇒ 5x + x = 90° + 60°

⇒ 6x = 150°

⇒ x = 150° ÷ 6

⇒ x = 25°

**∴ The correct answer is 25°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Complementary Angle Identities

For any angle θ, sin(90° − θ) = cos θ, tan(90° − θ) = cot θ, and sec(90° − θ) = csc θ.

Supplementary Angle Identities

For any angle θ, sin(180° − θ) = sin θ, cos(180° − θ) = −cos θ, and tan(180° − θ) = −tan θ.

Important Trigonometric Values

sin 30° = cos 60° = 1 ÷ 2 | sin 45° = cos 45° = 1 ÷ √2 | sin 60° = cos 30° = √3 ÷ 2.
